body.statement: For fixed \(K\) and \(q\), \(u_T(X)=T^{-1}D_qC_T(X)+\rho_T(X)\), where \(\sup_X\|\rho_T(X)\|_2=O_{K,q}(T^{-1})\). Under \(D_L^{\mathrm G}\), the normalized contribution of \(\rho_T\) and its covariance with \(D_qC_T(X^{\infty})/T\) vanish. Also \(T\|F_{T,q}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\to N_q\).
body.justification: The lemma closes the load-bearing difference between circular code identities and the estimator's exact finite linear-convolution denominators.
body.gap: Liang and Recht compare linear and circular convolutions asymptotically under independent assignment, but do not establish this coefficient-level remainder for the randomized block law.
body.consumer: It validates using finite Golay blocks in a trial that begins from zero prehistory rather than from an artificial periodic steady state.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(K,q\), and write \(C_h=C_{T,h}(X)\).  For \(0\leq \ell,j<K\), direct use of the zero-prehistory convention in \(\texttt{ass:zero-prehistory}\) gives
\[
(A^{\top}A)_{\ell j}
=\begin{cases}
T-\ell,&j=\ell,\\
C_{|\ell-j|}-E_{\ell j,T},&j\ne\ell,
\end{cases}
\tag{10}
\]
where \(E_{\ell j,T}\) is the terminal sum omitted by the shorter lagged column and contains exactly \(\min(\ell,j)\) binary products.  Thus \(|E_{\ell j,T}|\leq\min(\ell,j)\).  The diagonal contribution to \(A^{\top}A\Gamma_T^{-1}q-q\) cancels exactly.  Grouping the off-diagonal terms in (10) by \(h=|\ell-j|\) yields
\[
u_{T,\ell}
=\frac1T\sum_{h=1}^{d}
\left(q_{\ell-h}\mathbf1\{\ell\geq h\}
+q_{\ell+h}\mathbf1\{\ell+h<K\}\right)C_h+\rho_{T,\ell},
\tag{11}
\]
where every summand of the remainder is of the form
\[
q_j\left[\left(\frac1{T-j}-\frac1T\right)C_{|\ell-j|}
-\frac{E_{\ell j,T}}{T-j}\right].
\]
Since \(|C_h|\leq T-h\), \(|E_{\ell j,T}|\leq K\), and \(T-j\geq T-K+1\geq T/2\), there is a finite constant depending only on \(K,q\) such that
\[
\sup_X\|\rho_T(X)\|_2\leq \frac{c_{K,q}}{T}.
\tag{12}
\]
The coefficient in parentheses in (11) is precisely the entry of \(D_q\) from \(\texttt{def:block-covariance-objects}\), proving
\[
u_T(X)=T^{-1}D_qC_T(X)+\rho_T(X).
\]

Under \(D_L^{\mathrm G}\), \(\texttt{lem:golay-tensor-certificate}\) implies \(\mathbb E\|C_T\|_2^2=O_{L,d}(T)\).  From (12),
\[
T\mathbb E\|\rho_T\|_2^2=O(T^{-1})\to0,
\]
and Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
T\left\|\mathbb E\left[(T^{-1}D_qC_T)\rho_T^{\top}\right]\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\leq
T\bigl(\mathbb E\|T^{-1}D_qC_T\|_2^2\bigr)^{1/2}
 \bigl(\mathbb E\|\rho_T\|_2^2\bigr)^{1/2}
=O(T^{-1/2})\to0.
\]
This proves both asserted remainder negligibilities.

Finally, let \(S_\ell\) denote the lower shift by \(\ell\) coordinates on \(\mathbb R^T\).  Then
\[
TF_{T,q}=\sum_{\ell=0}^{d}\frac{Tq_\ell}{T-\ell}S_\ell.
\tag{13}
\]
This finite matrix is a compression of bilateral convolution with polynomial
\(Q_T(z)=\sum_{\ell=0}^{d}Tq_\ell z^\ell/(T-\ell)\).  Fourier diagonalization of bilateral convolution, proved by Parseval's identity, gives the upper bound
\[
\|TF_{T,q}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\leq\max_{|z|=1}|Q_T(z)|\longrightarrow N_q,
\tag{14}
\]
because the finitely many coefficients converge uniformly.  For the reverse bound, choose \(z_0\) maximizing \(|Q_q(z)|\) and use the normalized complex vector \(x_s=T^{-1/2}z_0^{-s}\).  On all but the first \(d\) output coordinates, (13) acts by multiplication by \(Q_T(z_0)\), up to an irrelevant unit-modulus factor.  Consequently
\[
\|TF_{T,q}\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2
\geq\frac{T-d}{T}|Q_T(z_0)|^2\longrightarrow N_q^2.
\tag{15}
\]
The operator norm of a real matrix is unchanged by complexification.  Equations (14)--(15) prove \(T\|F_{T,q}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\to N_q\).
